title: Ice Cube Says He Was 'Confused' by Chris Tucker Turning Down 'Next Friday,' Not Hurt
text:

Join MyComplex Unlock rewards SHOP STYLE SNEAKERS MUSIC SPORTS POP CULTURE BETS COVER STORIES VERZUZ WATCH COMMUNITY Pop Culture Ice Cube Says He Was 'Confused' by Chris Tucker Turning Down 'Next Friday,' Not Hurt
 The rapper and actor recalls Tucker's decision to leave the franchise.
 By Mark Elibert November 19, 2026 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Comments Comment Save Share Comments Comments (Photo by Paras Griffin/Getty Images) Key Takeaways
 Ice Cube said Chris Tucker left him “confused,” not hurt, when he declined to return as Smokey in Next Friday. 
 Cube said Tucker’s religious beliefs drove his refusal to promote weed smoking, a decision he respected that opened the door for Mike Epps as Craig’s cousin Day-Day. 
 New Line Cinema is developing Last Friday with One of Them Days director Lawrence Lamont, and Cube said production could run from April into June. 
 Ice Cube is reflecting on Chris Tucker 's decision to walk away from the Friday franchise, admitting that he struggled to understand why his former co-star didn't want to return for the sequel.
 During a Nov. 10 episode of Open Thoughts with Funny Marco, the rapper and actor recalled expecting Tucker to reprise his role as Smokey alongside his character, Craig, in 2000's Next Friday .
 "But I had figured it was going to be Craig and Smokey on the porch again, another adventure, and he didn't want to do it," Cube explained.

 Shop Ice Cube When Marco asked whether Tucker's decision hurt his feelings, Cube clarified that disappointment wasn't necessarily the issue.
 "I wouldn't say hurt my feelings. I was just confused. You know, like why you don't want to do it?" he said.
 Cube explained that he believes entertainers have a responsibility to consider what their fans want, especially when there's overwhelming demand for a sequel.
 "When the audience asks for it, I think we're damn near double obligated to try to make it happen," he said.
 According to Cube, the two discussed Tucker's potential return over the phone sometime around 1998 or 1999. Initially, he suspected money might be the problem.
 However, Tucker's concerns had more to do with his beliefs than his paycheck.
 "I don't want to push that image no more of smoking weed," Cube recalled Tucker telling him. 
 The Friday creator explained that Tucker "had got real religious as far as his views on things," adding that he ultimately "had to respect his reasons."
 With Smokey out of the picture, Cube reworked the sequel's storyline and introduced Craig's cousin Day-Day, played by Mike Epps.
 Rather than search for someone to imitate Tucker, Cube wanted "somebody who feel like my cousin, not somebody who is trying to be Smokey."
 Looking back, Cube believes Tucker's absence created opportunities for other memorable characters.
 "I'm glad he didn't do the movie because then I wouldn't have been able to work with Mike Epps," he said, adding, "You wouldn't have Uncle Elroy. You wouldn't have Pinky."
 Tucker previously addressed his decision on T.I.'s expediTIously podcast, explaining, "I never wanted to do sequels." 
 Now, more than two decades after Friday After Next , another installment is moving forward.
 Last Friday is in development at New Line Cinema, with One of Them Days director Lawrence Lamont attached to direct.
 Cube recently told Complex that production could begin in "April, May, and maybe a little of June."
